newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE TO AUCTION FRNS, 5-YR FIXED COUPON BOND.
newsitem.headline: GREECE TO AUCTION FRNS, 5-YR FIXED COUPON BOND.

text.p: Greece will auction seven-year FRNs and its first five-year fixed coupon bond next week, Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis told reporters.
Commissions routinely received by banks for state securities will be announced two days prior to the auction along with the tax status of the 5-year fixed coupon bonds, said Christodoulakis.
"The commissions will be determined two days prior to the auction by the public debt management committee and the tax status of the 5-year constant coupon bonds will be stated as usual," he said.
Greece planned to raise about one trillion drachmas worth of T-bills, FRNs, five-year fixed rate bonds and two-year zero coupon bonds domestically by end-96, said Christodoulakis.
About 300 billion drachmas of FRNs and five-year fixed rate bonds will be auctioned next week, he added without giving any hint of the breakdown between FRNs and five-year fixed coupon bonds.
About 350 billion drachmas worth of T-bills will be issued in early December and the balance will be auctioned at end-December to reach one trillion drachmas, he said.
Christodoulakis told a news conference that Greece would auction two-year zero coupon bonds at end-December in addition to other forms of state securities.
He added that the treasury was going to auction CPI index-linked bonds but declined to specify the timing of the issue and its maturities.
Christodoulakis expressed his optimism that CPI inflation would fall by more than two percent in 1997 and approach five percent.
"The cost of borrowing will follow a parallel course," he added.
The deputy finance minister announced plans to push forward with primary dealers in 1997 and set up a "flexible, management unit" made up of experts to manage the public debt.
He also announced the new 7-member public debt committee headed by himself. The committee will be supported by a permanent secretariat.

Bank of Greece Deputy Governor Takis Thomopoulos, Prime Minister's economic advisor Tassos Yannitsis, chairman of economic advisors at the national economy ministry Yannis Stournaras, debt specialist Christopher Sardelis participate in the committee.

Yannis Kousoulakos, secretary general at the finance ministry and special treasury secretary Dimitris Dritsas also participate in the committee. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
